_comment: Hand-curated landmark geometry keyed by OSM id. Every entry cites public sources. No LiDAR or non-public ortho was used.

376075961.name: 金茂大厦
376075961.notes: OSM only maps two shaft volumes (348 m and 382 m) plus a 420 m needle, which is not the 13-tier pagoda. Terraces follow the published 88-floor / 16-segment rule: each office segment is 2 floors (1/8 of the 16-story base) shorter than the one below, down to the hotel which starts at floor 53 (Wikipedia); hotel segments then drop one floor at a time (1/8 of an 8-level segment; SOM description quoted by the Skyscraper Museum). Heights are scaled to the published roof 385.5 m and tip 420.5 m (CTBUH / Wikipedia). Plan of each terrace is the OSM shaft (way 188377486) scaled about its centroid. Podium parts already in OSM are kept.

10691100.name: 上海环球金融中心
10691100.notes: The trapezoidal aperture is already modelled in OSM building:parts: the core stops at 430 m, the shoulders continue to 470 m, and a cap sits at 470–492 m (way 279942892). No geometric override.

165792123.name: 上海中心大厦
165792123.notes: OSM already has a stack of building:parts with min_height stepping from 90 m to 630 m and shrinking floor plates. No geometric override.

40778038.name: 东方明珠电视塔
40778038.notes: OSM maps many stacked parts (legs, sphere slices, spire) but they read as terraces rather than the two spheres. The viewer keeps a schematic sculpture from the published 468 m height and 50 m / 45 m sphere diameters (Wikipedia). This is not a LiDAR scan.

27498117.name: 外白渡桥
27498117.notes: OSM maps only a deck (bridge=yes, bridge:structure=truss) plus a man_made=bridge outline. The camelback through-truss is a schematic from the published two 52.178 m spans, 18.4 m overall width, 12.192 m main-truss spacing, 11 panels of 4.744 m and a 9.144 m mid-span height (zh.wikipedia / en.wikipedia). Placement follows the OSM centreline. This is not a LiDAR scan.

_waterfront.name: 外滩防汛墙与滨江平台
_waterfront.notes: Copernicus GLO-30 smears the quay into a long staircase. The rebuild sets a vertical-ish wall and a 14 m promenade at the published 6.9 m Wusong crest (Shanghai Water Authority 2024 table, reach 苏州河～复兴东路; also the 1989–1993 Bund rebuild described by Xinmin Weekly) and a short ramp down to a typical Bund street height of ~3.2 m (Xinmin Evening News 19 Nov 2007: the 5.72 m 1997 tide stood 2.5 m above the street). Not LiDAR.

jingan_temple.note: Schematic 庑殿重檐 copper roofs on OSM footprints. 大雄宝殿 height 26 m is from published sources below. 法堂 / 山门 / 钟楼 / 鼓楼 use typological eaves (no cited hall height used as a hard number). Not a scan, not LiDAR.
jingan_temple.fatang_height: typological (~28 m), not the 32 m figure from a weaker Sohu article

chenghuang_dian.note: Schematic 歇山顶 green-glazed roof on the City God Temple main hall. Height 16 m and depth 21.1 m from published sources. Plan is the OSM footprint (way 1576988166, area close to the published 13.7 × 21.1 m). Not a scan, not LiDAR. Yu Garden named halls stay OSM massing (no similarly cited hall heights used).

guanghua_towers.name: 复旦大学光华楼
guanghua_towers.note: Schematic height on the two OSM tower footprints (ways 498705155 and 498705156, each tagged building:levels=31). Official topping-out copy gives a total height of 142 m and 30-storey east/west main towers; the Chinese Wikipedia lists a 142 m tip and 140.2 m roof. Not a scan, not LiDAR. The large named outline (way 301674304, OSM 5 levels) is left as OSM massing — the cited 15-storey connector is not mapped as its own footprint, so it is not invented here.
